title: Why You Think Everyone in a Group Is the Same
hook: We naturally assume people in other groups are all alike.

narration.text: We naturally assume people in other groups are all alike.
This is called the outgroup homogeneity effect.
We see more diversity within our own group.
But we have less personal experience with other groups.
This leads us to generalise about them.
It is an unconscious mental shortcut.
Recognising this helps us challenge our assumptions.
Have you noticed this tendency in yourself?

description: It is easy to see the variety among our friends, but harder to spot it in people we do not know. This 'outgroup homogeneity effect' is a common psychological bias. Understanding it can help us form fairer impressions.
topic: Why we tend to assume people in a group are similar, known as the outgroup homogeneity effect.
